newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-DREAM DEBUT FOR VIERI AS ITALY BEAT MOLDOVA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DREAM DEBUT FOR VIERI AS ITALY BEAT MOLDOVA.

text.p: Christian Vieri made a dream debut for Italy on Saturday, scoring his country's 1,000th international goal as Italy cruised to a 3-0 World Cup qualifying win against Moldova.
Italy's fourth consecutive win in European group two takes them top on 12 points, three clear of England.

The game against Moldova proved as easy as it had looked on paper, with the game being virtually over as a contest after a brilliant 24th minute goal from Milan left back Paolo Maldini, son of team coach Cesare Maldini.

Making the most of space created by the movement of strikers Gianfranco Zola and Vieri, Maldini came off the left wing on a dizzying run which took him past three defenders before leaving Moldovan goalkeeper Denis Romanenco with no chance.
Playing to an enthusiastic 25,000-strong audience, Italy had started well and Maldini's goal set them up for a highly impressive win in the coach's home town.
The second goal came just before halftime when Vieri and Zola combined on the edge of the Moldova penalty area to set up a clear chance for Dino Baggio.
Baggio's shot was saved by Romanenco but Zola was on hand to slot in the rebound past the stranded goalkeeper.

Four minutes into the second half, Vieri made it a perfect night for Italy when he made the most of a Zola dummy to turn and drive an unstoppable left foot shot into the net for the 1,000th Italian international goal.
The first ever was scored by Pietro Lana 542 matches ago in a 6-2 win over France in Milan in 1910.
Speaking after the game, Vieri played down the significance of his goal -- dedicating it to himself.
"When I'd scored it, I didn't even realise that it was the 1,000th goal, I only understood its significance when the lads said it to me," he claimed.
"However, it was also a very important goal for me on my debut and I'm delighted, obviously".
Cesare Maldini was also very pleased.
"Moldova never caused us any problems, neither our defence nor our goalkeeper had much to do," he said.
"The important thing was to win, these are points which keep you going up the Group table."
"The goal scored by Paolo, my son, was a terrific goal not just in itself but also because it set the game up for us, but I was also very satisfied with Vieri's goal.
"The youngest player on the team had the honour of scoring Italy's 1000th goal. Not bad, is it?"
Italy play Poland next in Chorzow on Wednesday in another Group 2 qualifier.
Lazio defender Alessandro Nesta and Parma striker Enrico Chiesa will not be making the trip however.

Nesta pulled up in the first half with a leg muscle injury and was substituted in the 32nd minute. The player was returning to Rome for further medical tests and the Italian team doctor warned his could be a relatively serious problem.
Chiesa is not fully fit and has a twisted toe.
